newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee climbs back on short covering.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee climbs back on short covering.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures staged a slight rebound by the close on late short-covering after an earlier round of arbitrage selling against New York fizzled out, traders said.
Some players earlier unloaded their arbitrage positions against New York by selling in London.
"At the end, there were few shorts left in London and they decided to cover back," said one trader.
The sentiment was also drummed up by a fresh rally in New York on speculative buying.
By the finish, March stood at $1,275, up $13, after a low of $1,258 while May firmed $19 at $1,237.
Front-month January recovered from a low of $1,317 to end at $1,332, up $1. The closely-watched Jan/March spread narrowed to $57 from $70 on Wednesday.
Business was routine and overall volume was 4,172 lots, dominated by the nearby March.
Traders said news Colombia, Ivory Coast and Uganda agreed on the need to add 2.5 million 60-kg bags of coffee to be withheld by producers in first half 1997 had no immediate market impact.
They said the announcement so far had referred to agreement on the need, rather than an actual deal to tighten exports.
Meanwhile, the African delegation led by Ivory Coast would meet Brazilian coffee officials and exporters on Friday with the withholding plan likely to dominate discussion.
But Brazilian exporters gave a thumbs down to the plan. "I don't think that people will see as a reason to do this," one Brazilian exporter said.

Elsewhere, the U.S. Department of Agriculture is expected to release its semi-annual 1996/97 world coffee estimates after the close of New York trading on Friday but traders said no revisions from its last report in June were expected.
